knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=A cghCall/QDNAseq object or a data.frame containing segmented copy number values ;; data2=An optional data.frame containing discrete copy number calls, required if data is a data.frame and CNA-ass filtering is desired ;; filter=The filtering method for breakpoints, where 'CNA-ass' (default) filters out breakpoints flanked by copy number neutral segments ;; level=The resolution of statistical testing, either 'gene' or 'feature' ;; method=The FDR correction method, where 'Gilbert' is recommended for gene-level testing to account for discrete null distributions, and 'BH' is recommended for feature-level testing ;; fdr.threshold=The significance threshold used to filter and label recurrently affected genes in the breakpoint plot
- alternatives: CGHcall=Recommended Bioconductor package for preprocessing array-CGH data into cghCall objects ;; QDNAseq=Recommended Bioconductor package for preprocessing sequencing data into QDNAseq objects ;; biomaRt=Recommended for downloading and building custom gene annotation data.frames from Ensembl
- when_to_use: Use this analysis when you have copy number profiles (segmented and called) from a cohort of samples and want to identify specific genes recurrently disrupted by copy number breakpoints, which may indicate structural variations.
- pitfalls: The 'CNA-ass' filter requires discrete copy number calls (loss, neutral, gain, etc.) and cannot be run on segmented data alone ;; When using data.frames as input, the first five columns must be named exactly 'Chromosome', 'Start', 'End', and 'FeatureName' followed by sample columns ;; Running bpStats() may trigger harmless glm.fit warnings from underlying dependency packages which can be safely ignored

workflows.name: cghcall_object_pipeline
workflows.intent: Detect and analyze recurrent gene breakpoints starting from a preprocessed cghCall or QDNAseq Bioconductor object.
input: copynumber.data.chr20 (cghCall object containing segmented and called copy number data)
ens.gene.ann.hg18 (data.frame containing gene annotations with columns Gene, Chromosome, Start, End)
workflows.stages: 1. Load copy number data and extract breakpoints using getBreakpoints() ;; 2. Filter out non-CNA-associated breakpoints using bpFilter() ;; 3. Map genomic features to genes using addGeneAnnotation() ;; 4. Identify gene-associated breakpoints using bpGenes() ;; 5. Calculate cohort-based statistics at the gene level using bpStats() with the Gilbert method ;; 6. Calculate cohort-based statistics at the feature level using bpStats() with the BH method ;; 7. Plot breakpoint frequencies across the chromosome using bpPlot()
workflows.code:
library(GeneBreak)
library(CGHcall)
data( "copynumber.data.chr20" )
breakpoints <- getBreakpoints( data = copynumber.data.chr20 )
breakpointsFiltered <- bpFilter( breakpoints, filter = "CNA-ass" )
data( "ens.gene.ann.hg18" )
breakpointsAnnotated <- addGeneAnnotation( breakpointsFiltered, ens.gene.ann.hg18 )
featuresPerGene ( breakpointsAnnotated , geneName = "PCMTD2" )
geneFeatures <- geneInfo( breakpointsAnnotated )
breakpointGenes <- bpGenes( breakpointsAnnotated )
result_BreakpointGenes <- geneInfo ( breakpointGenes )
breakpointStatistics <- bpStats( breakpointGenes, level = "gene", method = "Gilbert" )
head( recurrentGenes( breakpointStatistics ) )
breakpointStatistics <- bpStats( breakpointStatistics, level = "feature", method = "BH" )
head( featureInfo( breakpointStatistics ) )
bpPlot( breakpointStatistics, fdr.threshold = 0.1 )

workflows.name: dataframe_input_pipeline
workflows.intent: Detect and analyze recurrent gene breakpoints starting from custom copy number data stored in standard R data.frames.
input: segmented.txt (tab-delimited file containing segmented copy number values with columns Chromosome, Start, End, FeatureName, and sample columns)
called.txt (tab-delimited file containing discrete copy number calls with columns Chromosome, Start, End, FeatureName, and sample columns)
ens.gene.ann.hg18 (data.frame containing gene annotations with columns Gene, Chromosome, Start, End)
workflows.stages: 1. Load segmented and called data.frames and extract breakpoints using getBreakpoints() ;; 2. Filter out non-CNA-associated breakpoints using bpFilter() ;; 3. Map genomic features to genes using addGeneAnnotation() ;; 4. Identify gene-associated breakpoints using bpGenes() ;; 5. Calculate cohort-based statistics at the gene level using bpStats() with the Gilbert method ;; 6. Calculate cohort-based statistics at the feature level using bpStats() with the BH method ;; 7. Plot breakpoint frequencies across the chromosome using bpPlot()
workflows.code:
library(GeneBreak)
library(CGHcall)
cgh <- copynumber.data.chr20
segmented <- data.frame( Chromosome=chromosomes(cgh), Start=bpstart(cgh), End=bpend(cgh), FeatureName=rownames(cgh), segmented(cgh))
called <- data.frame( Chromosome=chromosomes(cgh), Start=bpstart(cgh), End=bpend(cgh), FeatureName=rownames(cgh), calls(cgh))
breakpoints <- getBreakpoints( data = segmented, data2 = called )
breakpointsFiltered <- bpFilter( breakpoints, filter = "CNA-ass" )
data( "ens.gene.ann.hg18" )
breakpointsAnnotated <- addGeneAnnotation( breakpointsFiltered, ens.gene.ann.hg18 )
breakpointGenes <- bpGenes( breakpointsAnnotated )
breakpointStatistics <- bpStats( breakpointGenes, level = "gene", method = "Gilbert" )
breakpointStatistics <- bpStats( breakpointStatistics, level = "feature", method = "BH" )
bpPlot( breakpointStatistics, fdr.threshold = 0.1 )
